prompt: Security-review a FastAPI payment webhook endpoint that accepts POSTs from a third-party processor. It must verify HMAC signatures against a rotating secret, reject replayed deliveries using an event-id ledger, enforce idempotent processing under concurrent duplicate webhooks, and avoid leaking processor errors to clients. The current implementation verifies the signature AFTER parsing the JSON body and stores replay-ids in an in-memory dict. Identify the vulnerabilities in order of severity, then provide a corrected implementation with code.

Audit a Solidity constant-product AMM pool where the swap function updates user balances before settling internal reserves, prices swaps against a spot balance read from token.balanceOf(address(this)), and accepts arbitrary token donations. A liquidity bootstrapping front-end also quotes trades without slippage bounds. Enumerate the concrete attack paths (including first-depositor inflation and oracle spot-price manipulation), rank them by exploitability, and provide a hardened swap implementation with the correct ordering, price bounds, and reserve accounting.

Harden a multi-tenant Django REST application. The report endpoint builds filters by f-string concatenation into cursor.execute(), object permissions are checked only in the React frontend, SECRET_KEY and database credentials are hardcoded in settings.py committed to git, and staff status can be toggled through a mass-assignment-prone serializer. For each issue: name the CWE, demonstrate the exploit, and give the corrected code. The fix must cover parameterized queries, server-side object-level authorization, secrets management, and serializer field allowlisting.

Diagnose a Node.js 20 API service whose RSS climbs from 300MB to 4GB over ~48 hours until OOM-killed in Kubernetes. Heap snapshots taken 6 hours apart show growth concentrated in closures retained by an event-emitter registry and in Buffer objects from a response-logging middleware. Produce a step-by-step diagnosis plan: how to capture and diff heap snapshots in production safely, how to identify the retainer chain for closures and Buffers, how to confirm whether the emitter registry leaks listeners, and the likely code-level root causes with fixes.

A pytest suite passes in CI but intermittently fails on developer machines in exactly 3 of 240 tests; reruns usually go green. Failures correlate with machine load and with the developer's timezone. One test asserts on a formatted timestamp, another polls an async worker with sleep(2), and a third relies on dict iteration order over a set of fixture IDs. Apply a systematic debugging method: form hypotheses ranked by likelihood, design a minimal reproduction (including forcing ordering, freezing time, and stress-running), and prescribe deterministic fixes for each of the three tests.

A Python FastAPI service regressed from p50=80ms/p99=210ms to p50=85ms/p99=1900ms after a deploy, while CPU and memory look flat. Dashboards show a spike in DB connections and in query count per request. Design the investigation: which profiling instruments to attach under real traffic (continuous profiler, query tracing, connection-pool metrics), how to distinguish N+1 query patterns from pool saturation and lock contention, how to read the resulting flame graph, and propose fixes ranked by expected p99 impact including batching, indexing, and pool tuning.

Build a sliding-window rate limiter (per-key, configurable limit and window, distributed-safe interface) strictly test-first. Deliver: the ordered test list before any implementation, the first failing test, the minimal implementation to pass it, and the refactor step. Tests must cover boundary conditions (exactly at the limit, one over, window edge rollover), clock injection instead of real sleeps, concurrent acquisition from two coroutines, and key isolation. Show the red-green-refactor cycle explicitly for at least three increments and state what each refactor improved.

Design a Playwright E2E suite for a 4-step checkout flow (cart, address, payment, confirmation) that currently has 15% flake. Requirements: page-object model with typed locators, auth state reused via storageState instead of per-test logins, payment and shipping APIs stubbed via route interception with deterministic fixtures, network-idle-free waiting strategies, trace + video artifacts only on retry, and safe parallel execution across 8 workers with per-worker data isolation. Specify the config, the fixture hierarchy, and the quarantine policy for flaky specs.

QA a newly redesigned analytics dashboard (charts, tables, filters, dark mode) across desktop 1440px, tablet 768px, and mobile 390px. Produce a staged plan: read-only smoke crawl collecting console errors and failed requests, interaction tests for filter and drill-down flows, visual regression with masking of time-dependent widgets and a 0.1% diff threshold, and an accessibility pass (contrast, focus order, ARIA roles on the chart tooltips). Define the blast-radius rules (what never gets clicked), the baseline strategy for dark mode, and the exit criteria to sign off.

A 1,400-line OrderService class handles validation, pricing, tax, persistence, email, and audit logging, with 34 fields and direct SQL scattered through methods. Behavior must not change and there are no tests today. Lay out the refactoring campaign: characterization/golden-master tests first (including how to snapshot current SQL and email side effects), then the seam extraction order (which collaborator to interface first and why), incremental strangler steps each shippable behind the existing public API, and the target module boundaries. Specify how you prove behavior preservation at every commit.

Your 12-engineer team's modular monolith (Rails + Postgres) hits deploy-pain at 2 deploys/week and one hot module (realtime notifications) needs independent scaling. Leadership proposes a full microservices rewrite. Write the ADR that decides this: status, context with concrete forcing factors, the decision, at least three alternatives considered (including extracting only the notification module), consequences (positive and negative), and the reversal triggers that would invalidate the decision. Follow standard ADR structure and keep it decision-grade, not an essay.

A TypeScript multi-step wizard stores form state as `any` with `status: string`, guarded by `as` casts and non-null assertions; invalid transitions (submitting while step 2 is dirty, going back after payment) are runtime bugs. Model it as an exhaustive state machine: discriminated unions per step with per-step data requirements, branded/opaque IDs so UserId and OrderId cannot be confused, event-driven transitions with a `never`-checked exhaustiveness switch, and inference-friendly action types (no explicit any). Show the before/after type definitions and prove at compile time that the two invalid transitions above are unrepresentable.

Containerize a Python 3.12 + PyTorch inference service currently built as a single-stage 9GB image running as root. Requirements: multi-stage build with build wheels isolated from runtime, CPU-only torch with pinned hashes, non-root user with proper file ownership, HEALTHCHECK hitting /healthz with sensible intervals, layer ordering that maximizes cache hits across dependency-only changes, .dockerignore excluding datasets and .venv, secrets passed at runtime never baked as ENV, and a final image target under 2.5GB. Provide the Dockerfile and justify each layer decision.

Productionize a stateless Go API on Kubernetes: 3-10 replicas driven by CPU+custom-queue-depth autoscaling, graceful drain on deploy with zero dropped in-flight requests, correct liveness vs readiness vs startup probes for a service with a 20s cold cache warmup, resource requests/limits sized to avoid CPU throttling at p99, PodDisruptionBudget during node upgrades, and secrets from the cluster secret store mounted as files not env. Deliver the Deployment, HPA, PDB manifests and explain the probe threshold arithmetic and the termination-drain sequence.

Build a GitHub Actions pipeline for a TypeScript monorepo (pnpm, 3 apps, 8 libs): path-filtered CI per app, dependency + build caching keyed on lockfile, test matrix across Node 20/22 and shard-count 4, ephemeral preview environments per PR, deploy to production gated on environment approval using OIDC federation to the cloud (no long-lived keys), SBOM + artifact attestation on release, and required-status checks wired to the merge queue. Deliver the workflow YAMLs and explain cache-key design and the OIDC trust configuration.

A Postgres 16 reporting query over an 800M-row events table (filter by tenant_id, event_type, created_at range, then window-function rank and join to a 2M-row users table) takes 40s. EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows a Seq Scan, a sort spilling to disk, and stale estimates (planner expects 100 rows, gets 2M). Diagnose and fix: read the plan node by node, choose the right index strategy (composite vs partial vs covering with INCLUDE, and why order of columns matters), fix the estimate problem, decide whether partitioning by month is justified, and give the rewritten query with CTE/materialization choices explained.

Rename users.email to users.primary_email on a 120M-row Postgres table behind a live app running 8 replicas of mixed versions during the migration. Design the zero-downtime sequence: expand (add new column, dual-write with triggers or ORM events), backfill in bounded batches with lock-aware progress tracking, verify consistency, contract (flip reads, drop old column) only after all replicas run the new code. Cover lock behavior of each DDL statement, how to avoid long transactions and statement_timeouts during backfill, index rebuild strategy, and the tested rollback path at each stage.

Implement a distributed per-user rate limiter and hot-key cache in Redis 7 for an API fronted by 12 app servers. The limiter must be atomic across servers (no read-then-write races) with sliding-window semantics and fail-open vs fail-closed as an explicit choice. The cache layer must prevent stampedes on popular keys: single-flight locking with short-lived lock keys, TTL jitter, and stale-while-revalidate serving. Address pipeline vs Lua trade-offs for round-trip reduction, memory bounds via eviction policy per class of key, and what happens during a Redis failover (consistency of the counters).
